consequences: Future product, docs, registry, and branding work must use Wheel for the plugin and Bittie for the mascot; enforce naming consistency in reviews.
context: The future official Agent Harness plugin built on Bitty AI needs a product name of its own: bitty-ai is the repository name and Bitty is the terminal name. A mascot identity is also needed for future product, docs, and branding work.
decision_body: Name the official Agent Harness plugin Wheel. Name the mascot Bittie, a hamster.
rationale: Owner decision (2026-09-16). Wheel reads as the thing that turns agent work into motion and avoids colliding with the bitty-ai repo name and the Bitty terminal name. Bittie is a hamster, a natural wheel-runner, giving the mascot an intrinsic story link to the plugin name. Web checks found no dominant same-named Agent-Harness plugin and no same-named hamster mascot in the software space.
title: Official Agent Harness plugin named Wheel; mascot Bittie the hamster

consequences: Future product, docs, registry, and branding work must use Wheel for the plugin and Bittie for the mascot; enforce naming consistency in reviews.
context: The future official Agent Harness plugin built on Bitty AI needs a product name of its own: bitty-ai is the repository name and Bitty is the terminal name. A mascot identity is also needed for future product, docs, and branding work.
decision_body: Name the official Agent Harness plugin Wheel. Name the mascot Bittie, a hamster.
rationale: Owner decision (2026-09-16). Wheel is short for hamster wheel — the standard English term for the hamster running wheel as used by Wikipedia and the Oxford English Dictionary (also called running wheel / exercise wheel; tilted-disc variants are flying saucer / running disc). A hamster running on its wheel is the intrinsic story link between the mascot Bittie and the plugin name. Owner collision check: the only same-named software artifacts are Python wheel (the standard binary package format, .whl) and the npm wheel package (unified mouse-wheel event handling); neither collides in the Agent Harness plugin namespace. From now on, Wheel refers to the official core Agent Harness plugin.
title: Official Agent Harness plugin named Wheel (hamster-wheel provenance); mascot Bittie the hamster

consequences: Fan out: one design task (trait shape + call-site inventory) plus migration tasks per call site; add the lint gate to just check / CI.
context: AIQ-31 (Core/Lua split enforcement) is needs-evidence: the AI-Core (Rust) vs Lua plugin boundary is designed but nothing prevents cross-layer calls. Owner selection among (a) Rust trait boundary, (b) lint rule, (c) review checklist.
decision_body: Adopt (a)+(b): define a HostBoundary trait that all cross-layer calls must traverse (compile-time enforcement), plus a lint/regex gate banning direct cross-layer symbol references for day-to-day policing.
rationale: Owner selection (2026-09-17). The trait gives real compile-time enforcement; the lint catches drift cheaply between refactors. Review-checklist-only was rejected as no enforcement.
title: AIQ-31: Core/Lua split enforced by Rust trait boundary plus lint gate

consequences: Fan out: one docs task to draft the checklist into the canonical corpus; future promotions cite the checklist.
context: AIQ-32 (workflow-to-AI-Core promotion review) is needs-evidence: prototypes (AI-0047/48/49 style) are promoted to AI-Core by feel, with no stated bar. Owner selection among (a) promotion checklist, (b) per-case owner approval, (c) status quo.
decision_body: Adopt (a): a written promotion checklist (test coverage, fail-closed proof, no new dependencies, docs sync, independent review) gates every prototype-to-Core promotion.
rationale: Owner selection (2026-09-17). Explicit and executable; per-case approval does not scale and status quo defers the decision.
title: AIQ-32: prototype-to-Core promotion by checklist

consequences: Fan out: one design task for the wrapper API shape; implementation only after the shape is accepted.
context: AIQ-35 (git-primitive vs wrapper) is needs-evidence: version-control capability (blame/log/diff style) could shell out to git directly or traverse a controlled wrapper. Owner selection among (a) audited wrapper, (b) direct primitive invocation.
decision_body: Adopt (a): all git invocations traverse one audited wrapper (auditable, permission-scoped, mockable for tests).
rationale: Owner selection (2026-09-17). Direct invocation conflicts with the existing no-process-spawn constraint and is unauditable/untestable; the wrapper keeps the fail-closed tradition.
title: AIQ-35: version-control capability via audited git wrapper

consequences: Fan out: AI-0097 mechanism+tests task (envelope type, fallback path, tests); triage sync follows.
context: AIQ-46 (syntax-fallback disclosure format) is needs-evidence: when structured disclosure fails because the reader cannot parse the schema, no fallback format is defined. Owner selection among (a) plain-text fallback, (b) fixed minimal envelope, (c) fail-closed refusal.
decision_body: Adopt (b): define one permanently-readable minimal envelope (id + kind + text) used whenever the full schema is unreadable.
rationale: Owner selection (2026-09-17). Machine-parseable unlike plain text, consistent with the existing typed-error style; outright refusal was rejected for caller experience.
title: AIQ-46: syntax-fallback disclosure via minimal readable envelope

consequences: Record a cross-repo follow-up pointer (link when the host exposes a fence source); no new bitty-ai task from this remainder.
context: AIQ-2C remainder (cross-process fencing) is needs-evidence: AI-0092 proved only the in-process seam rule (WriterLease + check_writer). Transport, liveness/epoch election, and persistence for cross-process fencing have no owner. Owner selection among (a) bitty-host-owned fence state with bitty-ai consuming WriterLease, (b) bitty-ai self-hosted election + persistence.
decision_body: Adopt (a): fence state is owned by the bitty host (only the host has process visibility); bitty-ai consumes WriterLease and never builds election/transport/persistence.
rationale: Owner selection (2026-09-17). Self-hosting conflicts with the no-I/O constraint and duplicates host authority; (a) follows the authority-lives-with-host principle.
title: AIQ-2C remainder: cross-process fencing owned by the bitty host
